text: Ten fictional nonprofit programme passages, each with two changed-quantity, two reordered and two moved-negation quote variants for citation-checker testing.

passages.source_passage: At the mid-point of the Ubuntu Care Circle programme in Kesango District, 214 community caregivers were conducting home visits to 1,630 registered clients. Between March 2021 and September 2022, the share of clients reporting at least one visit per fortnight rose from 58% to 81%. Clients on antiretroviral therapy who received weekly visits missed fewer clinic appointments than those visited monthly. In exit interviews, clients rated emotional support more highly than material assistance. Referral records were incomplete in three of the eight wards, so the team could not verify whether every referral resulted in a clinic attendance. Supervisors accompanied caregivers on no more than two visits per quarter, which the evaluators consider too few.

variants.changed_quantity_2: the share of clients reporting at least one visit per fortnight rose from 58% to 87%
variants.reordered: Clients on antiretroviral therapy who received monthly visits missed fewer clinic appointments than those visited weekly

variants.moved_negation_2: No supervisors accompanied caregivers on more than two visits per quarter, which the evaluators consider too few

passages.source_passage: Volunteers at the Nyarko Basin school kitchens serve one hot meal each school day to pupils in Classes 1 to 6. Each portion should contain 150 grams of cooked grain and at least 40 grams of beans or fish. Always serve the youngest pupils before the head boys and girls who help in the kitchen. Volunteers may serve second helpings of grain but not of fish, because fish deliveries arrive only twice a week. Food that is cooked in the morning is not safe to serve after two o'clock. During the 2023 school year, 12 percent of kitchens ran out of cooking oil before the monthly delivery, so record stock levels in the ledger every Friday and send the sheet to the district coordinator.

passages.source_passage: The Lantern Savings Initiative now supports 86 village savings and loan groups across the Merida Hills, with a combined membership of 2,140. Total member savings reached 9.6 million shillings at the end of June 2024, a rise of 22% on the previous year. Women hold the chair position in most groups, while men more often serve as treasurer. Not every group has adopted the new ledger, but all have received it. The share-out in the Tolosa cluster was delayed because the treasurer was absent and the secretary held the only key. Staff did not attend the share-out meetings in person, as groups are expected to run them independently. The board is asked to approve a training budget for eleven new groups.

passages.source_passage: In 2023 the Clearwater Rural Partnership completed 18 boreholes and 340 household latrines in the Serengo and Kalu sub-counties, serving an estimated 7,900 people. Average walking time to the nearest water point fell from 47 minutes to 12 minutes. Households built latrines faster in Serengo than in Kalu, largely because Kalu soils are rocky. Monitors found that children used latrines less often than adults, so school sessions will be expanded. Committees that did not hold monthly meetings were slower to repair broken pumps. Hand-washing stations were installed at every school, but soap was not available at half of them during unannounced visits in November. We request that the second tranche fund soap supplies alongside pump spares.

variants.changed_quantity_2: Average walking time to the nearest water point fell from 47 minutes to 21 minutes

variants.moved_negation_2: Committees that did hold monthly meetings were not slower to repair broken pumps

passages.source_passage: The Sentinel Nets campaign distributed 48,500 long-lasting insecticidal nets across the Ardo Valley between 4 and 19 May 2024. Distribution teams allocated one net for every two people, rounding up for households with an odd number of members. Coverage surveys in June showed that 76% of children under five had slept under a net the previous night. Teams reached the lowland villages before the highland villages, because flooding had not yet closed the river roads. Not all households received the full allocation, but every registered household received at least one net. Two warehouses reported nets missing from sealed bales, but the losses were small enough that targets were not affected. Pregnant women are prioritised over school-age children in the mop-up round planned for September.

passages.source_passage: During 2023, the Haven Desk case management service in Mirafa Camp opened 1,212 new protection cases and closed 947. Unaccompanied children made up 31 percent of new cases, the highest share since the service began in 2019. Caseworkers were assigned to the most urgent cases before the routine follow-ups, using a three-tier risk score. Survivors of violence were referred to the medical team first and to legal aid second. Cases involving children were not handled by community volunteers but by qualified caseworkers. Every case was closed after a final home visit, but not every visit was completed within the target fourteen days. Your continued support will fund two additional caseworkers in 2024.

passages.source_passage: The Dryland Futures project distributed drought-tolerant sorghum and cowpea seed to 3,450 farming households in the Ketara Plains ahead of the 2024 short rains. Rainfall was 40% below the long-term average, yet sorghum plots yielded an average of 1.1 tonnes per hectare. Farmers planted sorghum on the upper slopes and cowpea on the valley floors, following extension advice. Women's groups managed the seed stores while village committees managed the seed fairs. Seed fairs were held in six villages, and the project did not purchase seed from outside the district. Not every household kept seed for the next season, but every household sold some surplus grain. Management recommends that the board approve expansion to two further wards in 2025.

variants.changed_quantity_2: Management recommends that the board approve expansion to four further wards in 2025

variants.moved_negation: Seed fairs were not held in six villages, and the project did purchase seed from outside the district
variants.moved_negation_2: Every household kept seed for the next season, but not every household sold some surplus grain

passages.source_passage: The Green Furrow farmer field school network was established in 2016 in the Bendara highlands and now includes 64 schools, each with 20 to 30 members. Most members farm less than one hectare and have not received formal extension advice. Field schools meet weekly throughout the growing season to compare conventional and improved practices on shared plots. In a 2022 internal review, members reported yield gains of 35% for beans and 12% for maize, although these figures have not been independently verified. Farmers trust advice from neighbours more than advice from radio programmes. Graduates did not stop attending after the first season, and many went on to become facilitators. The proposed project would extend the model to 40 new villages.

passages.source_passage: In the quarter ending 30 September 2024, outreach teams from the Sahana Mother and Child Project visited 52 hamlets in Rampura block. Community health workers registered 418 pregnant women, of whom 63% attended at least four antenatal check-ups. Facility births rose to 71 percent, compared with 58 percent in the same quarter last year. Teams referred high-risk women to the district hospital and routine cases to the sub-centre. Health workers prioritised first-time mothers over women with previous births during home visits. Women who did not attend the first check-up were less likely to deliver in a facility. Not every mother received a postnatal visit within 48 hours, but all mothers who delivered at home were visited within a week.

variants.moved_negation_2: Women who did attend the first check-up were not less likely to deliver in a facility

passages.source_passage: Each evening class in the Lamplight Literacy network meets three times a week for 90 minutes, from 6:30 pm. Classes should have no more than 25 learners; if enrolment is higher, ask the coordinator to open a second class. Begin each session with letter sounds before whole words, because most learners have never attended school. Never correct a learner in front of the group; speak to them quietly after the session. The network supplies exercise books, so learners should not be asked to buy them, but they should bring a pencil. When pairing learners, let the beginner turn the pages and the stronger reader point to the words. In the 2023 cycle, attendance dropped sharply when classes started late, so always arrive early.
